newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - ends off ahead of supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - ends off ahead of supply.

text.p: The U.S. municipal market closed down 1/8 to 1/4 point, following the U.S. Treasury market, in lackluster trading activity ahead of a busy slate of bond sales this week.
"The secondary was very light," said one municipal analyst.
"There was no secondary to speak of," said a trader.
The market ended overall down 1/8 to 1/4. High grade bonds were off slightly overall, an 02 in spots, market players said. Dollar bonds down 1/8 to 1/4 overall on the day.
Bid lists were out for the bid, totaling about $300 million.
"We should have some market on Tuesday," the analyst said.
Underwriters are expected to price a total of $3.7 billion in 115 sales this week, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Municipal bond sales for Tuesday are expected to total $1.8 billion in 37 sales. Negotiated offerings total $911 million in 14 sales, with a $316 million Palm Beach County, Fla., deal through Smith Barney topping the list. On the competitive side, 23 sales totaling $865 million are on the schedule, a $525 million California deal at 1200 EST is the largest.
An additional four sales totaling $51 million are on the possible calender, meaning underwriters have said they may price the bonds Tuesday, depending on market conditions.
In Monday's new issue action, Merrill Lynch & Co. won Mesa, Ariz.'s $24 million general obligation issue, at a net interest cost of 5.367 percent.
Goldman Sachs & Co won $94.7 million of Mesa, Ariz., utility system revenue bonds with a net interest cost of 5.610 percent.
